11.t: Working with data: weighing in water
q: What was the weight of the stone in air?
Calculate the upthrust on the stone.
The apple read 0.0 N in water. Explain what this means.
The upthrust equals its weight (2.0 N): the forces are balanced, so the apple floats.
The metal block has the smallest upthrust although it is the heaviest. Suggest why.
Upthrust depends on how much water is pushed aside (the object’s volume), not on its weight. The metal block is small but heavy (dense), so it pushes aside little water.
